decisions.reason: Korean is one flowing sentence; SOL’s period is choppier, and BASE’s connective does not change the action.
너랑 내가 pointedly echoes ‘you and I’ from the previous line; SOL’s ‘we’ flattens that challenge.
SOL’s ‘comrades in arms’ fits 전우, but ‘may not’ weakens the factual 피를 나누지는 않았고 and drops 똘똘 뭉친’s tightness.
decisions.replacement: “Comrades in arms who don’t share blood but can fight back-to-back? A lord-and-vassal relationship tightly bound by affection and trust?”

decisions.reason: ‘You’re determined’ is more idiomatic spoken English for 작정을 했구나 than ‘made up your mind.’
After ‘one hit,’ ‘it won’t kill me’ is the natural English for 설마 죽기야 하겠습니까.
‘Lay sprawled’ is tighter and matches the 널브러져 있는 state without extra padding.
방이 몇 갠데 means there are several rooms, not a large number; ‘so many’ overstates.
‘Leave him alone’ and the privy-then-found order are more natural for 내버려 둬 and 다녀와 보니.
‘Long story short’ is the English idiom for 결론부터 말하자면; BASE’s ‘cut to the conclusion’ is calqued.
SOL adds unsupported ‘sheer’ and more literary ‘emerged’; 나오자마자 and 노곤하게 stay closer in BASE.
Dropping ‘that’ is more natural spoken English without changing the challenge.
Tighter spoken cadence for 방심하다간, with the same warning and glossary sense of 은원.
거지꼴로 is overall appearance, not specifically dress; ‘looking like’ is more accurate.
‘The way he’s wired’ captures 성격이 돼먹은; SOL’s ‘how he is’ is flatter.
위장 is a disguise, not an ‘act,’ and 충분히 가능한 is possibility, not ‘easily.’
After conceding Mujin’s point, ‘Still’ is the natural contrastive for 하지만.
‘From side to side’ is translationese; English head-shakes are already lateral, so SOL naturalizes 절레절레 without changing the gesture.
‘Gratitude and grudges in the Murim’ is cleaner English for the same 은원 claim.
SOL imports ‘lunatics’ from the next line and weakens 놈들도 있을 with ‘might.’
처음 들어 보는 is first hearing, not ‘never imagined’; SOL also intensifies 많구나 to ‘full of.’
decisions.replacement: The world was a big place, and there were plenty of lunatics in it. I was surprised to hear something I’d never heard of, but I was also impressed by Mujin.

decisions.reason: 아주 기특해 is teasingly emphatic; ‘What a good boy’ keeps that, ‘Good boy’ flattens it.
나이쯤 is ‘around my age’; SOL drops the approximation.
‘Picking fights’ is the natural rendering of 시비 붙어서 싸우고, and ‘all the time’ still covers 일상다반사.
‘That’ continues the ‘Yes, that’ echo; SOL’s ‘it’ is only a synonym swap.
In a bookstore, ‘read for half a shichen’ is tighter without losing 책을 읽을.
‘A nostalgic look in his eyes’ is natural English for 추억에 잠긴 눈빛; ‘nostalgia in his eyes’ is stiffer.
The titles are spoken dialogue, and 세 바퀴 반 is ‘times around,’ but SOL replaces 등등 with an invented ‘all sorts of books.’
decisions.replacement: “*The Shop Assistant Becomes a Sword God, You Must Hurt to Become a Martial Artist, The Son of Murim Walks Three and a Half Times Around the Nine Provinces and Eight Wastes,* and so on… They were really interesting.”

decisions.reason: 마음먹었구나 is a decision; ‘inspired’ changes agency.
SOL drops 소장도 했습니다; he bought and kept them.
혼동하는구나 is a present realization, not a completed past-perfect act.
네가 본 소설 keeps ‘the novels you read’; SOL omits that.
The period gives 네, 다음 씹덕 a cleaner two-beat punchline.
노른자위 땅 is prime real estate, not ‘most valuable territory’; 목 좋기로 is a prime location.
decisions.replacement: Honghwa Inn stood in the heart of Taiyuan. Even in Taiyuan, known as Shanxi’s prime real estate, it was famous for its prime location.

decisions.reason: SOL adds unsupported ‘always’ and turns 심했다 into ‘hectic’; BASE keeps the natural-sight contrast.
‘Is a war breaking out?’ is more natural spoken English for 전쟁이라도 일어나나.
우뚝 멈췄다 is an imposing halt, not rolling to a stop, and 호화롭고 거대한 is luxurious and enormous.
족히 일백에 달하는 is at least a hundred; ‘nearly’ undercounts, and ‘at the top of his lungs’ overstates 힘차게.
Italics help mark 왕명, but SOL’s ‘drew…whispers’ loses 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
decisions.replacement: The short phrase *royal command* carried tremendous weight. On top of that, the thunderous cry of a hundred elite soldiers caused hushed voices to spill out from every direction.

decisions.reason: 하는 말이지 is ‘I’m saying,’ not asking; ‘His Highness’ correctly names the implicit subject of 요란하게.
decisions.replacement: “I know that much, but I’m saying this because His Highness has never made such a commotion before.”

decisions.reason: 큰 공을 세우다 is meritorious service in general; BASE’s ‘the Prince’ is an unsupported recipient.
나온다 / 나와 is specifically coming out, which BASE flattens to ‘coming.’
햇빛 아래 is beneath the sunlight, and 열기가 피어올랐다 is excitement rising, not ‘surged…into.’
Comma before sentence-final ‘too’ is only a style variant.
각기 means each of the five, which SOL’s ‘all worthy’ flattens.
군계일학 is the crane-among-chickens image, and 그 순간이었다 needs the interrupted-moment dash SOL drops.
decisions.replacement: Among them, Jin Taekyung’s presence stood out like a crane among chickens. At the very moment admiring gazes poured toward him as he stood tall in the center—

decisions.reason: With the moment-dash restored, inserting ‘Then—’ would double the beat.
물론이고…까지 and 이게 뭔가 하는 눈빛 are ‘not only…even’ and ‘what is this,’ which ‘baffled’ compresses away.
헛기침 here is a prompting social cough, which ‘pointed cough’ captures better than a mere throat-clear.
바닥에 엎어졌던 is face-down on the floor, and 일어나자 is getting up, not pushing himself up.
받들라 is an imperative; BASE’s ‘shall receive’ turns a command into a statement.
이번에 쓰러진 이는 여인이다 identifies the fallen person as a woman; SOL makes it a plain action.
순간 is ‘for a moment,’ which SOL drops.
‘I-I…’ is the standard English stammer for 과, 과인이.
내리는 from a royal speaker is bestowing, not issuing.
으득 is a crunch, but 깨물었는지 is uncertain; SOL makes the bite a definite fact.
decisions.replacement: This time, even the official couldn’t escape the disaster. Perhaps he had bitten his tongue, because a crunch came from his mouth, followed by blood streaming down his lips.

decisions.reason: 다른 의미로 is a different sense, not ‘very different.’
‘Strode confidently up’ is stronger, more natural English for 당당한 걸음으로 다가온.
‘Why don’t we’ is the natural collaborative suggestion for 안에서 하시죠.
말에 is Taekyung’s words; ‘suggestion’ is an unsupported narrowing.
피 튀어요 is present; blood is already hitting the clothes, not a future warning.
Splitting the excuse into cause then ‘that’s why’ matches Taekyung spinning 몸이 안 좋아져서 픽픽 쓰러진.
대답을 생각하느라 is thinking of an answer, not how to answer.
누가 대답할 줄 알고 is expecting someone else to answer, not waiting.
생각할 게 뭐가 있나요 is present-tense needling, not past.
Adding ‘him’ is only a synonym-level tweak; ‘told the truth’ already matches 사실대로 말하면.
입꼬리를 끌어당겼다 is forcing mouth-corners up, not a generic smile, and the split sentence reads more naturally.
미심쩍다 is dubious, not fully ‘suspicious,’ and SOL’s ‘still’ is not in 재차.
decisions.replacement: The official looked dubious as he asked another question.

decisions.reason: Addressing the group as ‘six of you’ is more natural than ‘six people’ without changing the count.
사람 꼴 is looking human; SOL’s ‘isn’t even in a condition’ is awkward and adds ‘even.’
decisions.replacement: *Because that one is in no condition to look human.*

decisions.reason: 사소한 시비가 붙어 is a minor clash/altercation, not a mere disagreement.
The official echoes 시비; ‘altercation’ keeps the same word as the prior line.
사람들 앞에 is in front of people, not ‘before anyone.’
되게 묘하네 is ‘really strange’; ‘incredibly’ intensifies it.
초대에 응하지 못하는 keeps the invitation; SOL drops it.
잘 말씀드려 보면 includes speaking well/properly, which SOL omits.
쑥대밭 is a ruined wasteland image; ‘turned upside down’ genericizes the idiom that the next line echoes.
Must echo 쑥대밭 as wasteland, and 무슨 말씀이십니까 is ‘what do you mean by that.’
이유를 들어 is citing as the reason, not blaming public order itself.
원망스럽군 is resenting/blaming the heavens, not cursing them.
대가족 is a big family; ‘huge’ overstates.
‘Squirming in my seat…when—’ naturalizes 좌불안석 and leads into 그때였다 better than dummy ‘it happened.’
‘At odds with the mood’ is more idiomatic English for 분위기에 안 맞는.
내려오는 is coming downstairs; ‘descending’ is too literary for Taekyung’s voice.
‘How about this?’ is the natural English pitch for 이렇게 하는 건 어떻습니까.
데려가면 is bringing someone along; dropping ‘along’ is only a cut, not an improvement.
아마도 그럴 거요 affirms ‘probably so’; SOL’s ‘probably not’ reverses or muddies the answer.
무려…씩이나 is ‘no less than’ a Peak master, not ‘full-fledged.’
